name: Graphene Ultracapacitor Tsuka Module
description:
A field-swappable graphene ultracapacitor bank packaged in a structurally complete tsuka (handle) assembly. The module slides off the nakago (tang) of a compatible blade in under two minutes and is replaced with a pre-charged spare in the same motion. Both energy harvesting systems — the TENG mune film and the PZT shingane core — route their output through electrode leads in the nakago to whichever module is currently mounted.

The capacitor bank uses ionic liquid electrolyte for maximum energy density in the available volume (15–20 cm³ of usable handle cavity). Ionic liquid electrolytes offer significantly higher voltage windows and lower vapor pressure than conventional aqueous or organic electrolytes, critical for a component that may experience combat-level mechanical stress. The graphene electrode structure provides the surface area density necessary to store approximately 200 millijoules in the available volume — the upper limit of what can be packaged into a tsuka without compromising grip ergonomics or structural integrity.

The module ships with tsukaito cord pre-wrapped. The cord shows a faint luminescence through the weave when the bank is significantly charged — a secondary charge indicator beyond the blade's hamon, visible when the blade itself is sheathed. The luminescence is passive: driven directly by bank voltage, cannot be spoofed.

Kyle carries one spare module. He rotates them the same way a shooter rotates magazines.
specifications: Capacitor chemistry: graphene/ionic liquid electrolyte ultracapacitor Rated storage: ~200 millijoules Usable volume: 15–20 cm³ Swap time: under 2 minutes in field conditions Electrode interface: compatible with Seo's custom nakago lead specification Outer wrap: tsukaito cord, standard blade-length application Luminescence: passive electroluminescent tsukaito indicator Operating temperature: -30°C to +85°C Shock resistance: rated to 150G (combat-grade)

cost.installation_labor: Field swap — no tools required. First installation alignment: Φ 200–400 bladesmith fitting to ensure nakago lead contact.
cost.availability: Cascades Energy Systems gray market via defense intermediaries. Not sold commercially. Lead time 1–3 weeks.
cost.notes: Kyle carries one spare module. Recommended minimum: two modules in rotation. Module lifespan: approximately 50,000 charge/discharge cycles before capacity degrades below 80% rated.
